free_tier.stated: The page offers an external link for 'any Document File of any SIZE'; no price, quota or daily count is stated.

per_object_cap.stated: The bot states 'any SIZE'; no number is published. Telegram's own file ceiling is 2 GB (4 GB with Premium).

retention.stated: unverified: the bot's page states no storage window or link lifetime.

egress.terms: No traffic allowance or price is stated on the bot's page.

interface_detail: A Telegram chat with the bot; the result is a link or a file delivered into the chat. No HTTP API is published.
tooling: Any Telegram client; a Telegram account is required to start the bot.
chaining: The large-file companion of @file2link_bot, which sends files above its 20 MB limit here; the link is HTTP, so it is read without the Bot API's 20 MB getFile cap.
binding_note: The only number that can be named from evidence is the per-file ceiling; the bot publishes no quota.

identity_cost.detail: A Telegram account, which is logged in with a mobile phone number; no key or card is asked on the bot's page.

reliability_note: Single-operator bot; the page directs problems to a FAQ inside the bot (behind a Telegram account), and shows 13 870 monthly users.
confidence_note: The description is the bot's own, read on its t.me page. Liveness of the backend needs a Telegram account and was not tested. Any paid tier of the bot is unverified: behind a sign-up (it is reached from inside the bot, with a Telegram account); the bot's page states no price.
